elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Clause c requires TrueLink to “defend” Client and its affiliates from “any third-party claim” within the enumerated categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims and resulting losses, costs, and expenses.
elements.evidence: Clause c requires TrueLink to “indemnify and hold harmless” Client and its affiliates from covered third-party claims and resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause c(i) covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, or any deliverable furnished by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Clause c(ii) covers third-party claims arising from “TrueLink's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Clause c(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content caused by TrueLink, an operative Vendor-causation standard for the specified data breach.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Clause c(iv) expressly covers “TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: Clause c requires the indemnified party to give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense.
elements.evidence: Clause c states that “the indemnifying party shall control the defense.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Clause c requires the indemnified party to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Clause a limits Client's indemnity to the extent claims arise from “Client Content,” which is the operative Customer-content trigger.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Clause a expressly identifies “Client's breach of applicable law” as the other permitted basis for Client's indemnity.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must exclude bases other than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Clause a uses the exclusive limitation “solely to the extent arising from Client Content or Client's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property infringement claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Clause c(i) provides an indemnity for third-party allegations that the specified services, Interface, or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Client appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Client specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include procuring the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued usage rights.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include modifying the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include replacing the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing equivalents.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP infringement remedies must include a refund if procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred element but omits the fallback exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap. It is not strictly minimal because clause c extends the new indemnity to additional indemnitees—directors, officers, employees, and agents—beyond the specified Customer and affiliates. It otherwise preserves the intended allocation without contradiction. Drafting quality is reduced by clause a's dangling reference to “the following” and terminal colon despite no ensuing list, clause b's duplicated and awkward “harmless” construction, and overlap between clauses b and c.
